subject: Culture
title: Placenta Rituals
description: A quick, practical guide to Placenta Rituals.

hook.text: In Māori tradition, the placenta is buried on ancestral land. It ties the child to the earth forever.

buildup.text: Many cultures treat the placenta as the baby's twin or guardian spirit. Disposal is never casual.

discovery.text: Navajo families bury the placenta near the home so the child will always return. Geography becomes destiny.

twist.text: In Western hospitals, the placenta is medical waste. A sacred object became a biohazard.

climax.text: What a culture does with the placenta reveals whether it sees birth as medical event or spiritual one.

punchline.text: Some cultures bury roots before the child can walk.

quiz.question: Why do Navajo families bury the placenta near the home?
options: So the child will always return home

details.summary: Many cultures treat the placenta as a sacred object requiring ritual handling — burying it to connect the child to their homeland, burning it, or planting a tree above it. In Maori culture, the word for land (whenua) is the same word for placenta, linking birth to earth.
details.whyItMatters: Placenta rituals reveal how cultures connect birth to earth, family, and identity. They challenge the Western medical view of the placenta as mere biological waste.
takeaways: Maori tradition buries the placenta to connect the child to their land
Many cultures plant a tree over the buried placenta
In Maori, 'whenua' means both placenta and land

faq.question: Why do some cultures bury the placenta?
faq.answer: Burial creates a literal, physical connection between the child and their homeland. In Maori tradition, burying the whenua (placenta) on family land anchors the child to their tūrangawaewae — their standing place in the world.

faq.question: What is lotus birth?
faq.answer: Lotus birth is the practice of leaving the umbilical cord attached to the placenta until it naturally detaches (3-10 days). Practitioners believe it provides a gentler transition for the newborn.
